questions.q: What real-world situation most commonly drives the need for data anonymization?
options: Cloning a production instance into a dev/test sub-production instance, where developers and testers don't need real customer PII
A field needing to be indexed for full-text search
A user requesting a password reset on their own account
Two ACLs evaluating in conflicting order on the same table
questions.explain: When production is cloned for development or testing, that clone carries all of production's real PII — anonymization replaces it with realistic fake data so that real data doesn't need to exist there at all.

questions.q: Why is it correct, not a flaw, that data anonymization is permanent and destructive?
options: Permanence is a limitation ServiceNow plans to remove in a future release
It's actually reversible if an admin requests the original values back
It's applied to environments where nobody legitimately needs the real value again, so destroying it removes the privacy liability with no way for it to leak back out
It only applies to fields that were never sensitive in the first place
questions.explain: Anonymization targets environments, like dev/test clones, where the real data genuinely isn't needed — permanent destruction is the safe and correct outcome there.

questions.q: How does data masking relate to the field-level ACLs covered in Chapter 2?
options: Masking replaces field-level ACLs entirely and makes them unnecessary
Masking only works on fields that have no ACL applied at all

It builds on the same idea but adds nuance: instead of a field being fully visible or fully hidden, masking shows an obscured version to unauthorized roles while the real value stays intact for authorized ones
Field-level ACLs and masking are unrelated and solve completely different layers of the stack
questions.explain: Masking extends the field-visible-or-not idea from field-level ACLs into a partial, role-based display of the value, rather than an all-or-nothing show/hide.

questions.q: What is the precise distinction between anonymization and masking?
options: Anonymization only applies to numeric fields, while masking only applies to text fields
Both permanently alter the underlying stored value in the same way
Anonymization permanently replaces the real value; masking hides the value from certain roles while preserving the real value underneath for authorized users
Masking is permanent and anonymization is reversible
questions.explain: Anonymization is destructive and permanent; masking is a non-destructive, role-based presentation control, and the real value is never changed.

questions.q: Which scenario calls for masking rather than anonymization?
options: Replacing every customer name in a load-testing dataset with randomly generated names
Permanently scrubbing a decommissioned sandbox instance before deleting it
Cloning a production instance into a QA test environment that will never need any real customer data
A production field where authorized roles must still see the real value, but other roles should only see an obscured version
questions.explain: Production needs the real data to remain available to the right people at all times — masking fits that need, while anonymization would destroy data the business still requires.
